svg.aria-label: Installing a book into the app — like opening an Obsidian vault, but signed
svg.title: Installing a book into the app — like opening an Obsidian vault, but signed

g.text: Installing a book into the app — like opening an Obsidian vault, but signed
Entitlement gates the download, not the reading. Files are verified on the device and mounted read-only; the same signed files also work from a USB stick or intranet.
1 · 'Open in CHITKALA' on a book's website opens the app's install sheet (registry, pack, edition).
2 · For licensed books the reader signs in; institution members use their university or hospital login.
3 · Cognito federates with the institution's IdP; membership becomes an entitlement.
4 · The app fetches the signed catalog and requests an install grant for chosen partitions.
5 · The Library API handles catalog, grant and update calls.
6 · It checks the entitlement (open, registered, paid, institutional) and records an offline lease.
7 · CloudFront serves immutable pack files from S3; a signed cookie limits access to the granted edition.
8 · Only missing content-addressed files are downloaded (a delta on updates).
9 · Offline clinics and classrooms install the same signed files from a USB stick or intranet registry.
10 · Signature, files digest and every hash are checked; the book is mounted read-only and indexes attach. Offline from here.
11 · A new revision in the catalog emits pack.revision.published.
12 · The notifier prepares the update notice, with erratum severity.
13 · Devices that opted in get a WebSocket notice; others see it at their next update check.
14 · A safety-critical erratum shows a banner on affected pages until the update is installed.
15 · Institutions can mirror the pack store into their own account; signatures keep mirrors safe.
